name: Barbell Bench Press
doThisNotThat: Touch the bar to the lower chest with forearms vertical, not the neck with elbows flared to 90°.
steps: Eyes under the bar, feet flat and slightly behind knees.
Grip ~1.5x shoulder width so forearms are vertical at the bottom.
Pinch shoulder blades down and back, small arch, butt on the bench.
Unrack to over the shoulders, lower 2-3 s to the sternum/nipple line with elbows ~45-60° from the torso.
Drive up and slightly back toward the rack line.
cues: Bend the bar into a U.
Push yourself away from the bar into the bench.
Drive the floor away with your feet.
homeSwap: Deficit push-up between two dumbbells, 3-s lowering, 1-s pause in the stretch; add a backpack when 15+ reps is easy.
note: Leg drive is a ground-up force lesson: screw the feet into the floor before unracking and the press gets a stable base, the same chain you need for a straight punch.
hardestPoint: Just off the chest (longest pec/delt moment arm).

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
doThisNotThat: Use a 30° bench, not 45°+, so the upper chest does the work instead of the front delts.
steps: Grip slightly narrower than flat bench; forearms vertical at the bottom.
Shoulder blades down and back, chest up to the bar.
Lower to the upper chest just below the collarbones.
Press up and slightly back over the shoulders.
cues: Push the bar toward the ceiling, not the rack.
Keep your chest tall to the bar.
homeSwap: Feet-elevated (decline) push-up on a chair, 3-s lowering; or floor-incline DB press with hips bridged.
note: Upper chest is the V-taper shelf; 30° gives most of the clavicular-head bias without turning it into a shoulder press.

name: Decline Bench Press
doThisNotThat: Use a mild 15-20° decline and touch the lower chest; steeper declines just shorten the range.
steps: Hook feet under the pads, set a 15-20° decline.
Lower 2-3 s to the bottom of the sternum.
Press straight up over the shoulders.
cues: Push the bar to the ceiling.
Bend the bar apart.
homeSwap: Push-up with hands on two dumbbells (neutral height) and feet on floor, 3-s lowering.
note: Shorter range than flat; treat it as a variation for elbows/shoulders that feel cranky on flat, not a main lift.

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
doThisNotThat: Grip at shoulder width, not hands touching; too narrow wrecks the wrists and shortens triceps range.
steps: Grip at shoulder width (index fingers about on the smooth/knurl edge).
Tuck elbows to ~30° from the torso.
Lower 2-3 s to the lower sternum.
cues: Drive the bar off your chest like a punch.
Snap the bar to lockout.
homeSwap: Diamond or close-grip push-up, 3-s lowering, feet elevated to add load.
note: Lockout strength is a straight-punch finish; finish every rep with a hard elbow extension.
hardestPoint: Mid-range as triceps take over (~90° elbow).

name: Paused Bench Press
doThisNotThat: Pause 1-2 s on the chest without sinking the bar in; stay tight and press from a dead stop.
steps: Set up like a flat bench.
Lower 2 s, pause 1-2 s motionless on the chest.
Keep shoulder blades pinned and legs tight through the pause.
cues: Freeze the bar on your chest.
Explode off the chest.
homeSwap: Paused deficit push-up: 2-s pause 1 inch off the floor.
note: Pauses kill the stretch reflex, so you learn to produce force from zero; useful for the arm-first sequencing problem because you must stay braced.

name: Spoto Press
doThisNotThat: Stop 1-2 inches above the chest and hold 1 s, staying tight; don't let the bar drift toward the face.
steps: Lower 2-3 s and stop an inch above the chest.
cues: Hover the bar over your shirt.
Push yourself into the bench.
homeSwap: Push-up with a 1-s hover one inch off the floor.
note: Builds control in the bottom position where flat feet and loose bracing usually leak force.

name: Larsen Press
doThisNotThat: Feet off the floor and legs straight; it trains upper-body stability, so use ~10-15% less than your bench.
steps: Lie on a flat bench, legs extended and feet hovering.
Lower 2-3 s to the chest staying centered.
Press without wobbling side to side.
cues: Keep the bar level like a tray.
Press yourself into the bench.
homeSwap: Floor press with a light DB, legs extended.
note: No leg drive means no hiding; reveals left/right imbalances quickly.

name: Barbell Floor Press
doThisNotThat: Let the upper arm rest on the floor for a full stop, then press; no bouncing elbows off the floor.
steps: Lie on the floor under the bar in a rack at ~arm-length height.
Lower until triceps touch the floor, pause 1 s.
cues: Push the bar to the ceiling.
Snap to lockout.
homeSwap: DB floor press with the heaviest dumbbells you have, 3-s lowering.
note: Shoulder-friendly lockout work; great on days your shoulder feels beat up from sparring.

name: Flat Dumbbell Bench Press
doThisNotThat: Lower until the dumbbells are level with the chest for a deep stretch, then press up and slightly in.
steps: Kick the dumbbells up from the knees as you lie back.
Dumbbells at a ~30° angle (pinkies slightly in), elbows ~45-60°.
cues: Push the dumbbells toward the ceiling.
Drive the floor away.
homeSwap: Deficit push-up between two dumbbells, 3-s lowering, 1-s pause in the stretch; add a backpack when 15+ reps is easy.
note: Dumbbells let each arm work alone, which exposes the side that fires late; lead with the weaker arm's rep count.

name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
doThisNotThat: Set 30°, not 45°; press up over the upper chest, not out in front of the face.
steps: Dumbbells start at the upper chest, forearms vertical.
Lower 2-3 s to a deep stretch, then press.
cues: Push yourself into the bench.
Punch the dumbbells to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Feet-elevated (decline) push-up on a chair, 3-s lowering; or floor-incline DB press with hips bridged.
note: Upper-chest growth for the V-taper; the deep stretch is where most of the growth stimulus is.

name: Decline Dumbbell Press
doThisNotThat: Mild decline (~15°) and a full stretch; don't go so steep that blood rushes to your head.
steps: Set a 15° decline and anchor the feet.
cues: Push the dumbbells to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Push-up on dumbbells with hands slightly below shoulder level.
note: Optional variation; keep it if it feels better on the shoulders than flat.

name: Neutral-Grip Dumbbell Press
doThisNotThat: Palms facing each other and elbows tucked ~30°; it's the most shoulder-friendly press, use it when shoulders are sore.
steps: Lie on a flat bench, palms facing each other.
Elbows tucked to ~30° from the torso.
Lower 2-3 s until DBs touch the chest sides.
cues: Punch the dumbbells up.
Push the floor away.
note: The tucked elbow path matches a straight punch more closely than a flared bench.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Bench Press
doThisNotThat: Keep both shoulders on the bench and resist the twist; it's an anti-rotation core drill plus a press.
steps: One DB in one hand, other hand holds the bench edge or rests on the hip.
Feet wide and screwed into the floor.
Lower 2-3 s, press without rolling toward the weight.
cues: Keep your chest square to the ceiling.
Drive the floor away.
homeSwap: Single-arm push-up negatives from the knees.
note: Anti-rotation under load is the same trunk job as staying square when punching with one hand.

name: Machine Chest Press
doThisNotThat: Set the seat so handles line up with mid-chest, and take a deep stretch; machines let you push near failure safely.
steps: Adjust the seat so handles are at mid-chest height.
Back flat on the pad, shoulder blades back.
Press out, lower 2-3 s to a full stretch.
cues: Push the handles away from you.
Keep your back glued to the pad.
homeSwap: Deficit push-up between two dumbbells, 3-s lowering, 1-s pause in the stretch; add a backpack when 15+ reps is easy.
note: Stable path = safe to take the last set to failure, good for the looks side without risking the shoulder.

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
doThisNotThat: Position the bench so the bar touches the lower chest on a vertical line.
steps: Place bench so the bar path hits lower chest.
cues: Push yourself into the bench.
homeSwap: Deficit push-up between two dumbbells, 3-s lowering, 1-s pause in the stretch; add a backpack when 15+ reps is easy.
note: Fixed path removes stability demand; use it for hypertrophy volume, not for athletic carryover.

name: Smith Machine Incline Press
doThisNotThat: Bench at 30° and positioned so the bar hits the upper chest, not the neck.
steps: Set bench to 30° under the bar.
Check the bar meets upper chest at bottom.
cues: Push the bar toward the ceiling.
homeSwap: Feet-elevated (decline) push-up on a chair, 3-s lowering; or floor-incline DB press with hips bridged.
note: Easy to push near failure safely for upper-chest volume.

name: Push-Up
doThisNotThat: Body in one straight plank and elbows ~45° with a full lockout and protraction at the top, not a sagging hips half-rep.
steps: Hands just outside shoulder width, fingers spread.
Squeeze glutes, ribs down: straight line head to heels.
Lower 2-3 s until chest is a fist from the floor.
Push the floor away and reach the shoulder blades apart at the top.
cues: Push the floor away.
Screw your hands into the floor.
homeSwap: Already home-ready; load it with a backpack or slow it to 4-s lowering.
note: Serratus "push-up plus" at the top builds the shoulder blade stability a punch needs.

name: Incline Push-Up
doThisNotThat: Use the incline to get full range with perfect form, not to do sloppy fast reps.
steps: Hands on a bench or counter.
Lower chest to the edge, 2-3 s.
cues: Push the bench away.
homeSwap: Hands on a couch or counter.
note: Good fatigued finisher; lower the surface as you get stronger.

name: Decline Push-Up
doThisNotThat: Feet on a chair 30-45 cm high; keep the plank rigid and touch the chest, not the face.
steps: Feet on a chair or bench, hands on the floor.
Lower 2-3 s, chest to the floor line.
cues: Push the floor away.
note: Home substitute for incline pressing; upper chest for the V-taper.

name: Diamond Push-Up
doThisNotThat: Hands under the sternum and elbows tucked back; flared elbows turn it into a wrist and elbow ache.
steps: Hands together forming a diamond under the sternum.
Lower 2-3 s, elbows brushing the ribs.
cues: Push the floor away.
Snap the elbows straight.
homeSwap: Already home-ready; elevate feet to load more.
note: Home triceps builder; lockout snap carries to punch extension.

name: Archer Push-Up
doThisNotThat: Shift weight onto the bending arm while the other stays straight; it's a progression toward a one-arm push-up.
steps: Lower toward one hand, other arm straight.
cues: Push the floor away with the bent arm.
note: Unilateral loading at home when dumbbells are too light.

name: Wide Push-Up
doThisNotThat: Hands only ~1.5x shoulder width; super-wide stresses the shoulder more than it builds the chest.
cues: Push the floor away.
note: Slightly more pec stretch; keep elbows under ~60°.

name: Pseudo-Planche Push-Up
doThisNotThat: Hands by the hips with fingers turned out and shoulders leaning well past the hands.
steps: Hands at waist level, fingers out.
Lean shoulders forward past the wrists.
cues: Lean your shoulders past your hands.
Push the floor away.
note: Hard bodyweight overload for the front delts when dumbbells are light; build up wrist tolerance first.

name: Ring Push-Up
doThisNotThat: Turn rings out at the top (RTO) and keep them close to the body at the bottom.
steps: Lower 2-3 s, rings by the ribs.
Press and turn the rings out at the top.
cues: Turn the rings out at the top.
homeSwap: Push-up with hands on two towels on a smooth floor (slow, controlled).
note: Instability trains shoulder stabilizers; good for combat.

name: Weighted Push-Up
doThisNotThat: Load until 6-12 reps is hard; a heavy backpack turns push-ups into a real strength lift.
steps: Backpack with books or a plate on the upper back.
cues: Push the floor away.
homeSwap: Backpack loaded with books or water bottles.
note: Best home chest overload with light dumbbells.

name: Pike Push-Up
doThisNotThat: Hips high and head travels in front of the hands, making a tripod; not a sloppy push-up with hips raised.
steps: Hands shoulder-width, hips high in an inverted V.
Lower 2-3 s, head forward of hands.
cues: Push the floor away.
Head through at the top.
homeSwap: Already home-ready; elevate feet on a chair to progress.
note: Home overhead pressing; build toward handstand push-ups.

name: Handstand Push-Up
doThisNotThat: Start with partials or negatives against a wall; full reps only once you can do 12+ elevated pike push-ups.
steps: Kick up to a wall handstand, hands 15-20 cm from the wall.
Lower 3 s to a pad under the head.
cues: Push the floor away.
note: Requires control upside down; skip if neck or wrists hurt.

name: Barbell Overhead Press
doThisNotThat: Squeeze glutes and move the head back then through, pressing straight up; no lean-back into a standing incline press.
steps: Bar on front delts, grip just outside shoulders, forearms vertical.
Feet hip-width, screw the feet, squeeze glutes.
Press the bar up, moving the head back just enough.
Head through at lockout, bar over the mid-foot.
cues: Push yourself away from the bar.
Drive the bar to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Standing single-arm DB press or pike push-up.
note: Ribs down and glutes on keeps the spine stacked so pressing power isn't lost through a banana back.

name: Push Press
doThisNotThat: Dip 10-15 cm straight down and drive through the legs; the arms only finish what the legs start.
steps: Dip straight down, knees forward, torso upright.
cues: Drive the floor away.
Throw the bar to the ceiling.
homeSwap: DB push press with the heaviest dumbbells.
note: Teaches legs-first sequencing: hips and legs lead, arms finish. That's the fix for your arm-first habit.

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
doThisNotThat: Bench at 80-85°, not 90°, and lower to ear level with elbows slightly in front of the body.
steps: DBs at shoulder height, elbows ~30° in front.
cues: Push the dumbbells to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Already home-ready; pike push-ups if dumbbells are too light.
note: Shoulder size adds to the V-taper.

name: Standing Dumbbell Shoulder Press
doThisNotThat: Screw the feet, squeeze the glutes, and press without leaning back.
cues: Push the dumbbells to the ceiling.
note: Standing version adds core and foot stability.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Overhead Press
doThisNotThat: Stay square and don't lean away from the dumbbell; the trunk resists the side bend.
steps: Stand tall, one DB at the shoulder.
Press up without shifting the hips.
cues: Push the dumbbell to the ceiling.
Stay tall.
note: Light dumbbells feel heavier one at a time; useful home overload.

name: Arnold Press
doThisNotThat: Rotate the palms out as you press, not after; a smooth turn hits front and side delts together.
steps: Start DBs at chin height, palms facing you.
As you press, rotate palms to face forward.
cues: Turn and push the dumbbells to the ceiling.
note: More time under tension with light dumbbells.

name: Landmine Press
doThisNotThat: Press up and forward along the arc and reach at the top; it's the best press for cranky shoulders.
steps: Bar end at shoulder height, staggered stance.
Press up and forward to lockout.
Reach the shoulder blade forward at the top.
cues: Drive the bar to the ceiling and forward.
Push the floor away.
homeSwap: Half-kneeling single-arm DB press at a 45° angle.
note: The angle matches the line of a punch; add a hip turn and it becomes a landmine punch.

name: Z Press
doThisNotThat: Sit on the floor, legs straight; without the backrest you must press from a stacked trunk.
steps: Sit on the floor, legs straight.
cues: Push the weight to the ceiling.
note: Exposes stiff hips and thoracic spine; good test of overhead mobility.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
doThisNotThat: Seat set so handles start at ear level; full range and controlled lowering.
steps: Adjust seat so handles are at ear height.
cues: Push the handles up.
note: Safe to take near failure for hypertrophy.

name: Behind-the-Neck Press
doThisNotThat: Skip it unless your shoulder mobility is excellent; front press gives the same gains with less risk.
steps: Only if you can raise arms overhead without arching.
Lower bar just to ear level behind the head.
cues: Push the bar up.
note: With your all-over stiffness, this is not recommended; use a front press.

name: Dumbbell Fly
doThisNotThat: Elbows slightly bent and locked, lower to a deep stretch, then hug a tree; not a press.
steps: Lie flat, DBs above chest, palms facing.
Lower 3 s in an arc to chest level.
cues: Hug a big tree.
note: Stretch position under load is the growth trigger; finish with lengthened partials.

name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
doThisNotThat: Bench at 30° and arc out to a stretch level with the chest.
cues: Hug a tree.
note: Upper-chest isolation for the V-taper.

name: Cable Crossover (High-to-Low)
doThisNotThat: Pulleys high, step forward, and sweep down to hip height so the lower pecs do the work.
steps: Sweep down and in to meet at hip level.
cues: Bring your hands together in front of your belly button.
homeSwap: DB fly on a slight decline (feet elevated floor fly).
note: Tension through full range where DB flies drop off at the top.

name: Cable Fly (Mid)
doThisNotThat: Pulleys at chest height; meet hands at sternum and pause 1 s.
steps: Sweep forward, hands meet at sternum.
cues: Hug the tree.
note: Full-range tension builds pec size.

name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
doThisNotThat: Pulleys low, sweep up to eye height to hit upper chest.
steps: Sweep up and in to eye level.
cues: Scoop your hands up to eye level.
note: Upper chest focus.

name: Pec Deck
doThisNotThat: Set the seat so handles are at chest height and control a deep stretch.
steps: Seat so handles are at mid-chest.
cues: Bring your hands together in front of you.
note: Easy and safe to push to failure.

name: Svend Press
doThisNotThat: Crush the plates together the whole set; squeeze hard, not heavy weight.
steps: Stand, squeeze two plates or a DB between palms at the chest.
Press forward to arms' length, keep squeezing.
cues: Crush the plates together.
note: Low-equipment pump finisher.

name: Chest Dip
doThisNotThat: Lean forward ~30° and go to ~90° elbow; don't sink to an extreme stretch if shoulders are stiff.
steps: Grip dip bars, lean torso forward 30°.
Lower 2-3 s until upper arms are parallel.
cues: Push the bars down to the floor.
homeSwap: Dip between two sturdy chairs, feet on the floor for assistance.
note: Big upper-body builder; respect stiff shoulders and stop at parallel.

name: Triceps Dip
doThisNotThat: Stay upright with elbows back; keep shoulders down, not shrugged.
cues: Push the bars down.
homeSwap: Chair dip with feet on floor.
note: Lockout strength for punches.

name: Bench Dip
doThisNotThat: Keep hips close to the bench and stop at 90°; deeper strains the front of the shoulder.
steps: Hands on bench edge, fingers forward.
cues: Push the bench down.
note: Limit depth; front shoulder is vulnerable here.

name: Ring Dip
doThisNotThat: Turn rings out at the top and keep them close to the body; only once you have 10 clean bar dips.
steps: Support on rings, arms straight, rings turned out.
cues: Push the rings to the floor.
note: Very high stabilizer demand.

name: Assisted Dip Machine
doThisNotThat: Use only enough assistance to get 8-12 clean reps.
steps: Kneel on the pad, set assist weight.
cues: Push the handles down.
note: Bridge to bodyweight dips.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
doThisNotThat: Lift out to the sides with a slight forward lean and stop at shoulder height; don't swing or shrug.
steps: Stand, slight lean forward, DBs at sides.
Raise out to sides, elbows slightly bent.
cues: Push the dumbbells out to the walls.
note: Side delts widen the shoulders; key V-taper muscle.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
doThisNotThat: Cable behind the body at hand height gives tension at the bottom where dumbbells give none.
steps: Pulley at the lowest setting, cable behind you.
Raise out to the side to shoulder height.
cues: Push your hand to the wall.
homeSwap: DB lateral raise lying on side (side-lying raise).
note: Loads the lengthened position.

name: Lean-Away Lateral Raise
doThisNotThat: Hold a post and lean away; lowers the bottom angle for more stretch.
steps: Hold a post with one hand, lean away.
cues: Push the dumbbell to the wall.
homeSwap: Hold a doorframe and lean away with a DB.
note: Lengthened bias for the side delt.

name: Machine Lateral Raise
doThisNotThat: Line up shoulder joint with the machine pivot.
steps: Adjust seat to align shoulders with pivot.
Raise arms out to shoulder height.
cues: Push the pads out.
note: Safe to push to failure.

name: Seated Dumbbell Lateral Raise
doThisNotThat: Sitting kills the body swing; use lighter weight and strict reps.
steps: Sit on a bench, DBs at sides.
cues: Push the dumbbells out to the walls.
note: Strict reps with light home DBs.

name: Y-Raise
doThisNotThat: Raise in a Y at ~30° from the head with thumbs up; light weight.
steps: Lean forward or lie face down on an incline bench.
Arms in a Y, thumbs up.
cues: Reach your thumbs to the ceiling.
note: Lower traps keep shoulder blades healthy for overhead work.

name: Lu Raise
doThisNotThat: Raise out to the sides all the way overhead, thumbs up; very light weight.
steps: Stand tall, light DBs at sides.
Raise out to sides and continue overhead.
cues: Reach to the ceiling.
note: Full-range overhead raise trains mobility and shoulder health.

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
doThisNotThat: Usually unnecessary: pressing already hits the front delts. Do it only if they lag.
steps: Raise DBs in front to eye height.
cues: Push the dumbbells forward.
note: Low priority for you; presses cover it.

name: Wide-Grip Upright Row
doThisNotThat: Grip wide and stop at chest/upper-ab height; narrow grip to the chin pinches the shoulder.
steps: Pull up leading with the elbows.
Stop when elbows reach shoulder height.
cues: Lead with your elbows to the ceiling.
homeSwap: DB upright row with wide hands.
note: Side delt builder; stop if any pinch.

name: Rope Triceps Pushdown
doThisNotThat: Pin elbows to the ribs and split the rope apart at lockout; no shoulder involvement.
steps: Push down and split the rope at the bottom.
cues: Split the rope apart at the bottom.
homeSwap: Overhead DB extension or diamond push-up.
note: Stasinaki 2018 found no clear difference vs overhead work; mix both.

name: Straight-Bar Pushdown
doThisNotThat: Elbows still, push the bar to the thighs.
steps: Bar on high pulley, overhand grip.
cues: Push the bar to your thighs.
note: Heavier loading than rope.

name: V-Bar Pushdown
doThisNotThat: Neutral-ish grip is easiest on the wrists; still pin the elbows.
cues: Push the bar to your thighs.
note: Wrist-friendly option.

name: Single-Arm Cable Pushdown
doThisNotThat: One arm at a time, elbow pinned, full lockout.
cues: Punch the handle down to the floor.
note: Fixes side-to-side imbalances.

name: Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
doThisNotThat: Face away from the stack and let the hands go deep behind the head for a full long-head stretch.
steps: Rope on low or mid pulley, face away.
Staggered stance, elbows up by ears.
Extend forward and up to lockout.
cues: Punch the rope forward and up.
note: Maeo 2022: overhead position grew triceps more than the same extension with arms at the sides.

name: Two-Hand Overhead Dumbbell Extension
doThisNotThat: Elbows point forward and in; lower the DB deep behind the head.
steps: Sit tall, hold one DB with both hands overhead.
cues: Push the dumbbell to the ceiling.
note: Long head grows in stretch (Maeo 2022).

name: Single-Arm Overhead Dumbbell Extension
doThisNotThat: Light DB, elbow pointing up, lower behind the head.
steps: Sit tall, DB overhead in one hand.
cues: Push the dumbbell to the ceiling.
note: One arm makes light home DBs heavier.

name: EZ-Bar Skull Crusher
doThisNotThat: Lower the bar behind the head, not to the forehead, so the long head is stretched.
steps: Lie on a bench, EZ bar over the chest.
cues: Push the bar to the ceiling.
note: Behind-head version adds lengthened bias.

name: Dumbbell Skull Crusher
doThisNotThat: Neutral grip, lower the DBs beside the head.
cues: Push the dumbbells to the ceiling.
note: Wrist-friendly.

name: JM Press
doThisNotThat: Hybrid of close-grip press and skull crusher; bar travels toward the chin.
steps: Lower bar toward chin with elbows forward.
cues: Push the bar to the ceiling.
note: Heavy triceps overload.

name: Dumbbell Triceps Kickback
doThisNotThat: Upper arm parallel to the floor and still; lock out fully and squeeze 1 s.
steps: Hinge or brace on a bench.
cues: Push the dumbbell back to the wall.
note: Finishing work; short-range at the stretch.

name: Tate Press
doThisNotThat: Elbows flare out and DBs touch the chest; light weight.
steps: Bend elbows outward to touch DBs to chest.
cues: Push the dumbbells to the ceiling.
note: Unusual angle for triceps variety.

name: Barbell Curl
doThisNotThat: Elbows still at the sides; curl up without swinging.
cues: Pull your hands toward your shoulders.
note: Full extension at the bottom loads the stretch.

name: EZ-Bar Curl
doThisNotThat: Angled grip is easier on the wrists; same strict elbows.
cues: Pull hands to shoulders.
note: Wrist-friendly barbell curl.

name: Alternating Dumbbell Curl
doThisNotThat: Supinate (turn pinky up) as you curl and lower fully.
steps: DBs at sides, palms facing in.
Curl one up, turning palm up.
cues: Turn the pinky to the ceiling.
note: Supination fully trains biceps.

name: Supinating Dumbbell Curl
doThisNotThat: Start neutral and rotate to palm-up through the top.
cues: Turn the pinky up.
note: Supination is half the biceps' job.

name: EZ-Bar Preacher Curl
doThisNotThat: Armpits at the top of the pad and lower to nearly straight under control.
steps: Sit with armpits on the pad top.
cues: Pull the bar to your chin.
homeSwap: DB curl on an incline bench (chest-supported).
note: Hardest at the stretched bottom: great for growth.

name: Dumbbell Preacher Curl
doThisNotThat: One arm at a time on the pad; full stretch.
cues: Pull dumbbell to shoulder.
homeSwap: Arm over the back of a chair.
note: Unilateral preacher.

name: Machine Preacher Curl
doThisNotThat: Align elbow with machine pivot.
steps: Upper arms flat on the pad, armpits at its top edge.
Lower 3 s to nearly straight arms.
cues: Pull handles to shoulders.
note: Safe failure.

name: Spider Curl
doThisNotThat: Chest on an incline bench, arms hanging straight down; strict top-range squeeze.
cues: Pull dumbbells to shoulders.
note: Peak contraction emphasis.

name: Concentration Curl
doThisNotThat: Elbow braced on inner thigh; full range.
cues: Pull dumbbell to shoulder.
note: Strict isolation.

name: Cable Curl
doThisNotThat: Step back slightly so tension stays on at the bottom.
cues: Pull the bar to your shoulders.
note: Constant tension.

name: Bayesian Cable Curl
doThisNotThat: Face away from the pulley with the arm behind the body; maximum long-head stretch.
cues: Pull the handle to your shoulder.
note: Lengthened bias.

name: Drag Curl
doThisNotThat: Drag the bar up the body with elbows moving back.
steps: Pull elbows back as you curl.
cues: Drag the bar up your shirt.
note: Short-head emphasis.

name: Reverse Curl
doThisNotThat: Overhand grip, wrists straight.
cues: Pull knuckles to the ceiling.
note: Forearm size and grip.

name: Cross-Body Hammer Curl
doThisNotThat: Curl across the body toward the opposite shoulder.
cues: Pull thumb to opposite shoulder.
note: Brachialis emphasis.

name: Zottman Curl
doThisNotThat: Curl up palms up, rotate at the top, lower palms down slowly.
cues: Turn the pinky up on the way up.
note: Forearm eccentric work.

name: 21s Curl
doThisNotThat: 7 bottom-half, 7 top-half, 7 full reps; use light weight.
cues: Pull hands to shoulders.
note: Metabolite finisher for pump.

name: Chin-Up as Biceps Builder
doThisNotThat: Underhand grip, full hang to chin over bar; chin-ups train biceps heavily.
cues: Pull the bar to your chest.
homeSwap: Inverted row underhand under a sturdy table.
note: A compound that covers biceps.

name: Wrist Curl
doThisNotThat: Let the bar roll to the fingertips, then curl up.
cues: Curl the bar to the ceiling.
note: Grip for grappling.

name: Reverse Wrist Curl
doThisNotThat: Palms down, light weight.
steps: Sit, forearms on thighs, palms down, wrists just past the knees.
Let the weight lower 2 s to a full wrist bend.
Lift the knuckles as high as they go, pause 1 s.
cues: Lift your knuckles.
note: Elbow health balance.

name: Wrist Roller
doThisNotThat: Arms straight out, roll the weight up and down.
cues: Roll the rope up.
note: Forearm size.

name: Plate Pinch
doThisNotThat: Pinch two plates smooth side out.
steps: Put two plates together, smooth sides out.
Pinch with fingers on one side and thumb on the other.
Stand tall and hold 20-40 s, then switch hands.
cues: Crush the plates.
note: Thumb strength for grips.

name: Dead Hang
doThisNotThat: Relax the shoulders to decompress, hold 30-60 s.
steps: Grip the bar overhand, hands shoulder-width.
Lift feet and let the body hang straight.
Relax the shoulders up by the ears and breathe slowly for 30-60 s.
cues: Squeeze the bar.
homeSwap: Towel-door hang only if safe; otherwise farmer hold.
note: Shoulder decompression plus grip.

name: Farmer Hold
doThisNotThat: Heaviest DBs, tall posture, 30-45 s.
steps: Deadlift the heaviest dumbbells you own to your sides.
Stand tall: ribs down, shoulders back, tripod feet.
Hold 30-45 s without letting the handles roll in your fingers.
cues: Crush the handles.
note: Grip for clinch.

name: Fat-Grip Training
doThisNotThat: Wrap a towel around the handle for thickness.
steps: Wrap a hand towel tightly around each handle until it is ~5 cm thick.
Do curls, holds or rows as normal.
Stop the set when your grip slips before the target muscle fails.
cues: Crush the handle.
note: Grip transfer.

name: Rice Bucket Training
doThisNotThat: Open, close, and twist hands in a bucket of rice.
cues: Push the rice apart.
note: Cheap hand health.

name: Neck Flexion
doThisNotThat: Light load, slow, nod chin down first.
steps: Lie on a bench, head off the end.
cues: Nod your chin toward your chest.
note: Neck strength for boxing.

name: Neck Extension
doThisNotThat: Face down, head off bench, slow.
steps: Lie face down, head off bench.
Light plate on back of head.
cues: Look at the wall ahead.
note: Neck strength for absorbing punches.

name: Neck Lateral Flexion
doThisNotThat: Ear to shoulder, slow and light.
steps: Lie on side, head off bench.
cues: Push your ear to the ceiling.
note: Side-to-side neck stability.

name: Neck Harness Extension
doThisNotThat: Start very light; slow reps.
cues: Look ahead.
note: Boxing neck strength.

name: Neck Isometrics
doThisNotThat: Push head into hand with 50-70% effort, no movement.
steps: Sit or stand tall, chin slightly tucked.
Place a hand on the forehead and push the head into it at 50-70% effort for 10 s with no movement.
Repeat with the hand on the back and each side of the head.
cues: Push your head into your hand.
note: Safe daily neck work.

name: Plate Neck Curl
doThisNotThat: Towel under plate, light.
steps: Lie on bench, head off end.
cues: Nod chin to chest.
note: Neck for boxing.

name: Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Press
doThisNotThat: Hold the bell upside down and crush the handle; a wobble means your shoulder isn't stacked yet.
steps: Light KB upside down at the shoulder.
cues: Crush the handle.
Push the bell to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Hold a DB vertically by one end and press slowly.
note: Teaches the rotator cuff to stabilize, protecting the shoulder for punching and overhead work.

name: Half-Kneeling Landmine Press
doThisNotThat: Down knee on the same side as the pressing arm, glute squeezed; press up and forward.
steps: Kneel on the pressing-side knee, other foot forward.
Press up and forward, reach at the top.
cues: Drive the bar up and forward.
note: Glute-to-shoulder diagonal is the same sling a rear-hand punch uses.

name: Seated Barbell Overhead Press
doThisNotThat: Back on an upright bench, press over the head without arching off the pad.
cues: Push the bar to the ceiling.
note: Removes leg help; strict shoulder strength.

name: Cable Y-Raise
doThisNotThat: Cross the cables low and raise in a Y with thumbs up.
steps: Raise arms up and out in a Y.
cues: Reach your thumbs to the ceiling.
homeSwap: DB Y-raise lying face down on an incline.
note: Shoulder blade health plus side-delt growth.

name: Cable Triceps Kickback
doThisNotThat: Hinge forward, upper arm fixed beside the torso, extend to full lockout.
steps: Low pulley, handle in one hand.
Hinge, upper arm parallel to floor.
cues: Push the handle back to the wall.
note: Tension stays on at lockout unlike dumbbells.

name: Reverse-Grip Pushdown
doThisNotThat: Underhand grip, elbows pinned, lighter weight.
steps: Straight bar on high pulley, underhand grip.
cues: Push the bar to your thighs.
note: Variation if wrists hurt on overhand.

name: Rope Hammer Curl
doThisNotThat: Rope on low pulley, neutral grip, elbows still.
cues: Pull the rope to your shoulders.
note: Forearm and arm thickness.

name: Machine Triceps Extension
doThisNotThat: Line elbows up with the pivot; full stretch.
steps: Adjust seat so elbows line up with pivot.
cues: Push the pads down.
note: Safe failure.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
doThisNotThat: Pause the upper arms on the floor 1 s, then press.
steps: Lower DBs until triceps touch floor, pause 1 s.
cues: Punch the dumbbells to the ceiling.
note: Shoulder-friendly at home; good on sparring-sore days.

name: Hindu Push-Up
doThisNotThat: Flow from down-dog through a swoop to up-dog; smooth, not rushed.
steps: Swoop chest forward close to floor.
cues: Swoop your chest under a low bar.
note: Combines pressing with thoracic and hip mobility, good for stiffness.
